FOREWORD 


This standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the 
Neurosurgery Instruments, Implants and Accessories Sectional Committee had been approval of the Medical 
Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. 


This standard was originally published in 1978. This revision aligns the cross references to the latest standards 
and incorporates the revised designation for stainless steel. After publication of this standard, IS 8799 : 1978 
stands withdrawn. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 8799 : 2023 


Indian Standard 
KERRISON RONGEUR 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard specifies material, dimensions and 
other requirements for kerrison rongeur-used in 
neurosurgery. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standard given below contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard. At the time of publication, the 
editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based 
on this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent edition of 
these standards. 


IS No. Title 


IS 6603 : 2001 Stainless steel bars and flats — 
Specification (first revision) 


IS 7531 : 1990 Methods for testing of corrosion 
resistance of stainless steel 
surgical instruments (first 
revision) 


3 MATERIAL 
3.1 Shaft and Arms 


The material shall be made of stainless steel 
conforming to designation X40Cr13 of IS 6603. 


3.2 Spring 


The spring shall be made of stainless steel 
conforming to designation X30Cr13 of IS 6603. 


3.3 Screws and Pins 


The material shall be made of stainless steel 
conforming to designation X20Cr13 of IS 6603. 


4 TYPE, SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 


4.1 The kerrison rongeur shall be of the following 
two types: 

a) Type 1— Having up-bite jaws, and 

b) Type 2 — Having down-bite jaws. 
4.2 Shape, sizes and dimensions for kerrison rongeur 


shall be as shown in Fig. 1 unless otherwise agreed 
to between the purchaser and the supplier. Up-biting 


tip angled at 45° may also be provided, if required 
by the purchaser, other requirements remaining 
unchanged. 


4.3 A deviation of + 2.5 percent shall be allowed on 
all dimensions. 


4.4 Joint 
Shall be box type as shown in Fig. 1. 


5 MANUFACTURE, WORKMANSHIP AND 
FINISH 


5.1 The rongeur shall be of a symmetrical and 
balanced construction. 


5.2 The biting-tip end shall be either flat or slightly 
curved in both up-bite and down-bite jaws. 


5.3 The movable jaw shall slide evenly and without 
any stiffness, jerks or play. The tip of the movable 
jaw shall have a sharp edge and shall be recessed to 
provide a good cutting action. The tips shall register 
accurately to facilitate efficient shearing. The slot 
and sliding arrangement shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the supplier. 


5.4 The screws shall be well formed. 


5.5 The rongeur shall be free from surface defects 
like scales, burrs, pits, seams, cracks, etc. on its 
internal as well as external surfaces. The gripping 
portion of the handle shall be matt finished or 
suitably grooved to facilitate gripping. The rongeur 
shall be polished bright and passivated. 


6 HEAT TREATMENT 


The Rongeur shall be suitably hardened and 
tempered to give a uniform hardness of 500 HV to 
590 HV. 


7 TESTS 
7.1 Performance Test 


Bite a teakwood of 3 mm thickness with the rongeur 
jaws. This shall be done easily and cleanly. The test 
shall be repeated five times. On completion of the 
test, biting jaws as well as the rongeur as a whole 
shall show no sign of damage. 


IS 8799 : 2023 


7.2 Corrosion Resistance Test 


The rongeur shall show no sign of corrosion or 
staining, when tested in accordance with IS 7531. 


8 MARKING 
8.1 The kerrison rongeur shall be marked with the 


following information by etching or otherwise: 


a) ‘Manufacturer’s name, initials or recognized 
trade-mark; and 


b) The words ‘stainless steel’ or letters ‘SS’. 


IN DIRECTION H 


Extra Large Other dimensions for his size are under study and shall be included later on) 
(Type land 2) 


DOWN BITE SHAFT 


Tapp pe 
33 


8.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules 
and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
product(s) may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


9 PACKING 


As agreed between the purchaser and the supplier.

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Head (Publication & Sales), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MHD 07 (20238).
